title: Hypoalgesic Effect of Cervical Manipulation
brief_summary: This study evaluates the hypoalgesic effect of global and specific cervical joint manipulation in healthy individuals. At first the participants received one of the interventions and after 48 hours, the other.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* healthy subjects of both sexes
* without pain complaints in the last 90 days

Exclusion Criteria:

* previous spinal surgeries
* spinal canal stenosis
* vertebral fracture
* spondylolisthesis
* cancer
* acute infections
* hemorrhagic disorders
* active tuberculosis
* deep vein thrombosis
* osteoporosis
* rheumatic diseases
* metabolic diseases
* cardiorespiratory diseases
* smoking injury
* musculoskeletal injury
* use of pacemaker
* women in menstrual period
* pregnant women
* use of pain-killers in the last 48 hours
* use of anti-inflammatory drugs in the last 48 hours
* previous joint manipulation treatments
* aversion to cervical joint manipulation
* positivity in the vertebral artery test
* headache in the last seven days
